disposition: whole nut held constant in task
assessment: Rats consumed a hazelnut while drug conditions changed bracing and dodging. No separate oil or micrographia comparison.
Hazelnut oil odorized item lids in the cognition task. Paclitaxel and Cremophor control were the nociception contrast.

Leaf polyphenols tested in a hyperuricemia zebrafish model. No kernel oil or Parkinson motor symptom was tested.

disposition: existing dated primary paper with new claim link
assessment: Actual oral oil and a scheduled urine assay. Required fluid intake and timed collections make urinary excretion distinct from urgency.

Supplier and fixed seed oil are named; processing of the study lot is unavailable. Cell-based measurements do not measure clinical drooling or swallowing.

disposition: new outcome in same formulation research
assessment: Excised sheep tongue gravimetry and adhesiveness. No saliva output, oral intake, voice or clinical swallowing result.

disposition: verified exact pressing and differentiated outcome
assessment: Cold-pressed oral oil reduced experimental gastric lesions. Severity of pain was unmeasured.
Pain is background motivation. The study reports adhesion and histology endpoints, with no measured pain or dietary oil effect.

disposition: measured fine digit function with mixed carrier
assessment: Hazelnut spread thinned with sunflower oil was shared. Digit-grip scores measure pharmacological recovery in spinal injury, without handwriting or isolated oil.
P192 reports pain after hazelnut-containing foods with anaphylaxis. Neither isolated oil, pain severity rating nor relation to Parkinson is established.
